/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.TraceLint
  The admission check of a trace written by hand (a reviewer's counterexample), before any rule is
  run on it. It reads the trace and, for the witness check, a grounding, a case's entities and one
  timestamp: no law, rule, formula, contract or reading parameter. Every check is exact, in
  rational arithmetic, with no tolerance: a written trace has no measurement noise, and its author
  is shown these rules. Traces a source records are never held to it.

  `checkTrace` requires:
  - identity: track, region and device ids unique within a scene; at most one measured relation
    per ordered pair of tracks within a scene; every reference a scene makes (`Scene.references`)
    names an entity of that kind present in the same scene, a sight-along-way entry names a
    highway, and an `entrance_of` entry names a lane, a roadway, a shoulder or a bicycle lane or
    path, or a kind refining one (`StructureKind.entranceCarriers`); every track a link names
    appears in some scene;
  - a static map: the same structures in every scene, each identical at every appearance; every
    device that does not move (`Device.mobile`) in every scene; a device identical at every
    appearance outside its state (`Device.staticPart`);
  - one representation of direction and control: a designated direction (`lane.direction`) is
    carried only by a structure a vehicle travels in (`directionKinds`: a lane, reserved lane,
    turn lane, bicycle lane or path, roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder; a centre turn lane
    carries none), and is not the zero vector; each carrier stands on its own, and carriers that
    overlap or cross may carry different directions. A device whose control is observed governs
    only the travel regions whose traffic it controls, or an intersection, read as control of the
    junction itself (`governedKinds`); never a highway, a controlled-access region or a region no
    vehicle travels in. Only a lane, a roadway, a shoulder or a bicycle lane or path, or a kind
    refining one, carries the intersection it is an approach to (`lane.enters_intersection`); a
    roadway, one-way roadway, shoulder or bicycle lane or path that carries one is a directed
    approach segment entering that one intersection, which the check cannot see, and a whole
    two-way roadway or bicycle path carries none. Only a stop line or a crosswalk
    lists the carriers whose entrance it marks (`entrance_of`). A place no carrier covers has no
    designated direction, a device whose `governs` is not written has no observed control, and a
    line whose `entrance_of` is not written has no observed entrances; none is filled in;
  - valid geometry: a boundary has at least three vertices, all distinct (the first is not
    repeated at the end), a non-zero area and no self-intersection; an extent's half-length and
    half-width are positive; a path length is not negative; a heading is not the zero vector; a
    supplied relation's `surface_gap` has no negative component (each is a distance between the
    bodies' nearest points, zero on contact or overlap);
  - geometric occupancy: a track whose occupancy is observed has a position, a heading and an
    extent, and in a scene with such a track every structure has a valid boundary, because a
    pair absent from `occupies` is read as not occupied. The pairs of such a track are not
    written by hand: `completeOccupancy` derives them, the pair (track, structure) exactly when
    the track's footprint (`footprint`) and the structure's boundary overlap as closed sets
    (`Geom.polygonsOverlap`), so touching counts and a body on the line between two lanes
    occupies both;
  - path length: between consecutive observations of a track's path length it never decreases,
    and its increase is at least the straight-line distance between the two positions;
  - heading against yaw rate: where a track's heading is the same direction at two consecutive
    scenes (parallel and not opposed, whatever the vectors' lengths), the yaw rate integrated
    between them, ω (t₁ − t₀) with the later sample's rate held over the interval before it, is a
    whole number of turns (a multiple of 360°).
  `checkReferences` is the identity part alone. A witness trace is held to the whole check, after
  `completeOccupancy`, as a reviewer's trace is.
  `checkWitness` requires that `at` is the timestamp of a scene, and that every grounded track and
  every entity of the case, with its declared kind, is present in that scene.

  Each message names the scene by its timestamp, the entity and the field.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Atoms
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Formula

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace TraceLint

private def dups {α : Type} [BEq α] (xs : List α) : List α :=
  (xs.filter fun x => xs.count x > 1).eraseDups
private def at_ (s : Scene) : String := s!"scene t={s.t}"
private def qs (q : Q) : String := if q.den == 1 then s!"{q.num}" else s!"{q.num}/{q.den}"
private def kindName : EntityKind → String
  | .track => "track" | .region => "region" | .device => "device"
private def reprStr {α : Type} [Repr α] (x : α) : String := toString (repr x)
private def orList (ks : List StructureKind) : String :=
  match ks.reverse with
  | [] => ""
  | [k] => k.toString
  | k :: rest => s!"{", ".intercalate (rest.reverse.map (·.toString))} or {k}"

/-- Whether an entity of this kind and id is present in the scene. -/
def present (s : Scene) (k : EntityKind) (id : Nat) : Bool :=
  match k with
  | .track => s.tracks.contains id
  | .region => (s.structure? id).isSome
  | .device => (s.device id).isSome

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Identity and references
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
private def identity (s : Scene) : List String :=
  (dups s.tracks).map (fun t => s!"{at_ s}: track {t} appears more than once in users")
  ++ (dups (s.structures.map (·.id))).map (fun r => s!"{at_ s}: structure id {r} appears more than once")
  ++ (dups (s.devices.map (·.id))).map (fun d => s!"{at_ s}: device id {d} appears more than once")
  ++ (dups (s.relations.map fun m => (m.a, m.b))).map (fun (a, b) => s!"{at_ s}: more than one relation for the ordered pair ({a}, {b})")
  ++ s.references.filterMap fun r =>
    if !present s r.kind r.id then
      some s!"{at_ s}: {r.place} names {kindName r.kind} {r.id}, which is not in this scene"
    else if r.structureKinds.isEmpty then none
    else if (s.structure? r.id).map (fun st => r.structureKinds.any (st.kind.refines ·)) == some true then none
    else some s!"{at_ s}: {r.place} names region {r.id}, which is not a {orList r.structureKinds}"

private def links (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  let all := (τ.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
  τ.flatMap fun s => s.links.flatMap fun (a, b) =>
    ([a, b].filter (!all.contains ·)).map fun t => s!"{at_ s}: links names track {t}, which appears in no scene"

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The static map and the devices
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
private def staticMap (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  match τ with
  | [] => []
  | s0 :: _ =>
    let ids0 := s0.structures.map (·.id)
    let first := fun (r : RegionId) => τ.findSome? (·.structure? r)
    τ.flatMap fun s =>
      let ids := s.structures.map (·.id)
      (ids0.filter (!ids.contains ·)).map (fun r => s!"{at_ s}: structure {r} is missing; the map is the same in every scene")
      ++ (ids.filter (!ids0.contains ·)).map (fun r => s!"{at_ s}: structure {r} is not in the first scene; the map is the same in every scene")
      ++ s.structures.filterMap fun st => match first st.id with
        | some st0 => if reprStr st0 != reprStr st then some s!"{at_ s}: structure {st.id} differs from its first appearance; every field of a structure is the same in every scene" else none
        | none => none

private def devices (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  let ids := (τ.flatMap fun s => s.devices.map (·.id)).eraseDups
  let first := fun (d : DeviceId) => τ.findSome? (·.device d)
  τ.flatMap fun s =>
    (ids.filterMap fun d => match first d with
      | some dv => if !dv.mobile && (s.device d).isNone then some s!"{at_ s}: device {d} is missing; a device that does not move is in every scene" else none
      | none => none)
    ++ s.devices.filterMap fun dv => match first dv.id with
      | some d0 =>
        if reprStr d0.staticPart != reprStr dv.staticPart then
          some s!"{at_ s}: device {dv.id} differs from its first appearance in a field that is not its state (its state is {String.intercalate ", " Device.stateFields}{if d0.mobile then ", position" else ""})"
        else none
      | none => none

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Representation: where a designated direction and a device's control are written
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The structure kinds a vehicle travels in that may carry a designated direction. A centre turn
    lane, shared by both directions, carries none. -/
def directionKinds : List StructureKind :=
  [.lane, .reservedLane, .turnLane, .bicycleLaneOrPath, .roadway, .oneWayRoadway, .shoulder]

/-- The structure kinds a device may govern: the kinds refining the travel region, the regions
    whose traffic it controls and an intersection, read as control of the junction itself and of
    nothing else. -/
def governedKinds : List StructureKind :=
  StructureKind.all.filter fun k => !k.isAbstract && k.refines .travelRegion

/-- The structure kinds that mark a carrier's entrance into an intersection. -/
def entranceKinds : List StructureKind := [.stopLine, .crosswalk]

/-- The structure kinds that carry an entrance into an intersection: those of
    `StructureKind.entranceCarriers` and every kind refining one of them. -/
def carrierKinds : List StructureKind :=
  StructureKind.all.filter fun k => StructureKind.entranceCarriers.any (k.refines ·)

/-- The kinds a region may have at each region argument of an atom or primitive, keyed by its Lean
    name and the argument's index in its full argument list: `some ks` where the field the name reads
    there is carried by, or may name, only a region whose kind is in `ks` (the lists this check and
    `Scene.references` hold the field to); `none` where a region of any kind may stand there. A class
    atom `st_<kind>` reads the label every region has and is `none`. -/
def regionArgKinds : List ((String × Nat) × Option (List StructureKind)) :=
  let refining := fun (ks : List StructureKind) => StructureKind.all.filter fun k => ks.any (k.refines ·)
  [(("st_lane_enters", 0), some carrierKinds),
   (("st_entrance_of", 0), some entranceKinds),
   (("st_entrance_of", 1), some (refining StructureKind.entranceCarriers)),
   (("st_lane_direction", 0), some directionKinds),
   (("dev_governs", 1), some governedKinds),
   (("st_sight_along_way", 1), some (refining StructureKind.sightWays)),
   (("prim_region_offset_along", 2), some directionKinds)]
  ++ ([("st_lane_enters", 1), ("rel_occupies", 1), ("st_road_edge_paved", 0), ("st_shoulder_paved", 0),
       ("st_median_or_divider_opening", 0), ("st_crosswalk_marked", 0), ("st_reserved_lane_class", 0),
       ("st_turn_lane_side", 0), ("st_parking_space_designation", 0), ("st_curb_zone_kind", 0),
       ("st_curb_zone_colour", 0), ("st_obstruction_kind", 0), ("st_lane_adjacency", 0), ("st_lane_adjacency", 2),
       ("st_lane_adjacency_left", 0), ("st_lane_adjacency_left", 1), ("st_lane_adjacency_right", 0),
       ("st_lane_adjacency_right", 1), ("st_lane_connectivity", 0), ("st_lane_connectivity", 1), ("st_on_way", 0),
       ("st_on_way", 1), ("st_lane_marking", 0), ("st_lane_marking_left", 0), ("st_lane_marking_right", 0),
       ("st_lane_adjacency_ordinal", 0), ("st_lane_adjacency_count", 0), ("st_lane_width", 0), ("st_curvature", 0),
       ("st_grade", 0), ("st_sight_distance", 0), ("st_parking_space_angle", 0), ("st_region_geometry", 0),
       ("st_region_geometry_distance", 1), ("prim_region_lateral_offset", 1), ("prim_region_offset_along", 1)]
      ++ StructureKind.all.map fun k => (s!"st_{k}", 0)).map (·, none)

private def representation (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  let firstStructure := fun (r : RegionId) => τ.findSome? fun s => (s.structure? r).map fun _ => s.t
  let firstDevice := fun (d : DeviceId) => τ.findSome? fun s => (s.device d).map fun _ => s.t
  τ.flatMap fun s =>
    (s.structures.flatMap fun st =>
      -- the map is static, so each structure is reported once, at its first appearance
      if firstStructure st.id != some s.t then []
      else match st.lane.bind (·.direction) with
        | none => []
        | some v =>
          (if directionKinds.contains st.kind then []
           else [s!"{at_ s}: structure {st.id} ({st.kind.toString}) carries lane.direction; only a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, bicycle lane or path, roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder does"])
          ++ (if Q.isZero v.1 && Q.isZero v.2 then [s!"{at_ s}: structure {st.id} lane.direction is the zero vector"] else []))
    ++ (s.structures.filterMap fun st =>
      if firstStructure st.id != some s.t || (st.lane.bind (·.entersIntersection)).isNone || carrierKinds.contains st.kind then none
      else some s!"{at_ s}: structure {st.id} ({st.kind.toString}) carries lane.enters_intersection; only a lane, a roadway, a shoulder or a bicycle lane or path, or a kind refining one, enters an intersection as an approach")
    ++ (s.structures.filterMap fun st =>
      if firstStructure st.id != some s.t || !st.entranceObserved || entranceKinds.contains st.kind then none
      else some s!"{at_ s}: structure {st.id} ({st.kind.toString}) carries entrance_of; only a stop line or a crosswalk marks an entrance")
    ++ s.devices.flatMap fun dv =>
      if firstDevice dv.id != some s.t || !dv.governsObserved then []
      else dv.governs.filterMap fun r => match s.structure? r with
        | some st =>
          if governedKinds.contains st.kind then none
          else some s!"{at_ s}: device {dv.id} governs structure {r} ({st.kind.toString}); a device governs the travel regions whose traffic it controls (a lane, reserved lane, turn lane, centre turn lane, bicycle lane or path, roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder) or an intersection"
        | none => none

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Geometry
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- What is wrong with a boundary, or nothing. -/
def boundaryErrors (poly : List Vec) : List String :=
  if poly.length < 3 then ["has fewer than three vertices"]
  else if !(dups poly).isEmpty then ["repeats a vertex (the first vertex is not repeated at the end)"]
  else if Q.isZero (Geom.area2 poly) then ["has zero area"]
  else if Geom.selfIntersects poly then ["intersects itself"]
  else []

private def geometry (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  let firstOf := fun (r : RegionId) => τ.findSome? fun s => (s.structure? r).map fun _ => s
  τ.flatMap fun s =>
    (s.structures.filterMap fun st =>
      -- a structure is static, so its boundary is reported once, at its first appearance
      if (firstOf st.id).map (·.t) != some s.t then none
      else match st_region_geometry_boundary s st.id with
        | some poly => match boundaryErrors poly with
          | [] => none
          | e :: _ => some s!"{at_ s}: the boundary of structure {st.id} {e}"
        | none => none)
    ++ (s.relations.filterMap fun m => match m.surfaceGap with
      | some (lon, lat) =>
        if Q.lt lon Q.zero || Q.lt lat Q.zero then
          some s!"{at_ s}: relation ({m.a}, {m.b}) surface_gap ({qs lon}, {qs lat}) has a negative component; each component is a distance between the bodies' nearest points, along and across a's heading, zero on contact or overlap"
        else none
      | none => none)
    ++ s.tracks.flatMap fun x =>
      (match kin_extent s x with
       | some (l, w, _) => if Q.le l Q.zero || Q.le w Q.zero then [s!"{at_ s}: track {x} extent: the half-length and the half-width must be positive"] else []
       | none => [])
      ++ (match kin_path_length s x with
       | some p => if Q.lt p Q.zero then [s!"{at_ s}: track {x} path_length {qs p} is negative"] else []
       | none => [])
      ++ (match kin_heading s x with
       | some h => if Q.isZero h.1 && Q.isZero h.2 then [s!"{at_ s}: track {x} heading is the zero vector"] else []
       | none => [])

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Occupancy, path length, heading against yaw rate
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The trace with the occupancy of every observed track derived from the geometry: in each scene,
    for a track in `occupancy_observed` whose footprint is defined, `occupies` holds the pair
    (track, structure) exactly when the footprint and the structure's valid boundary overlap as
    closed sets; what the trace listed for that track is replaced, every other pair kept. -/
def completeOccupancy (τ : Trace) : Trace :=
  τ.map fun s =>
    let derived := (s.occupancyObserved.filter (s.tracks.contains ·)).eraseDups.filter (footprint s · |>.isSome)
    let kept := s.occupies.filter fun (t, _) => !derived.contains t
    let made := derived.flatMap fun t => match footprint s t with
      | none => []
      | some fp => s.structures.filterMap fun st => match st_region_geometry_boundary s st.id with
        | some poly => if (boundaryErrors poly).isEmpty && Geom.polygonsOverlap fp poly then some (t, st.id) else none
        | none => none
    { s with occupies := kept ++ made }

private def occupancy (s : Scene) : List String :=
  let obs := (s.occupancyObserved.filter (s.tracks.contains ·)).eraseDups
  if obs.isEmpty then []
  else
    let bodies := obs.filterMap fun t =>
      if (footprint s t).isNone then
        some s!"{at_ s}: track {t} is in occupancy_observed but lacks a position, a non-zero heading or an extent, so its footprint is undefined"
      else none
    let unbounded := s.structures.filterMap fun st =>
      if (st_region_geometry_boundary s st.id).isNone then
        some s!"{at_ s}: structure {st.id} has no boundary; where occupancy is observed every structure needs one, since a pair left out of occupies is read as not occupied"
      else none
    bodies ++ unbounded

private def pathLength (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  let tracks := (τ.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
  tracks.flatMap fun x =>
    let obs := τ.filterMap fun s => (kin_path_length s x).map fun p => (s, p, kin_position s x)
    (obs.zip (obs.drop 1)).flatMap fun ((s0, p0, q0), (s1, p1, q1)) =>
      let inc := Q.sub p1 p0
      if Q.lt inc Q.zero then [s!"{at_ s1}: track {x} path_length {qs p1} is less than {qs p0} at t={s0.t}; it never decreases"]
      else match q0, q1 with
        | some a, some b =>
          if Q.lt (Q.mul inc inc) (Geom.normSq (Geom.vsub b a)) then
            [s!"{at_ s1}: track {x} path_length grows by {qs inc} m since t={s0.t}, less than the straight-line distance between its two positions"]
          else []
        | _, _ => []

/-- Whether two non-zero headings are the same direction: parallel and not opposed. -/
def sameDirection (a b : Vec) : Bool := Q.isZero (Geom.cross a b) && Q.gt (Geom.dot a b) Q.zero

/-- Whether an angle in degrees is a whole number of turns. -/
def wholeTurns (deg : Q) : Bool := deg.num % (360 * (deg.den : Int)) == 0

private def yaw (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  (τ.zip (τ.drop 1)).flatMap fun (s0, s1) =>
    s1.tracks.filterMap fun x =>
      match kin_heading s0 x, kin_heading s1 x, kin_yaw_rate s1 x with
      | some h0, some h1, some ω =>
        if !sameDirection h0 h1 then none
        else
          let turn := Q.mul ω (Q.sub (Time.ofTimestamp s1.t) (Time.ofTimestamp s0.t))
          if wholeTurns turn then none
          else some s!"{at_ s1}: track {x} keeps the heading it had at t={s0.t}, but its yaw rate turns it {qs turn}° over the interval (the rate at a scene is held over the interval before it)"
      | _, _, _ => none

/-- The identity and reference defects of a trace: what no adapter output can contain, whoever
    wrote it. Empty for a trace that passes. -/
def checkReferences (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  τ.flatMap identity ++ links τ

/-- Every inconsistency of a written trace. Empty for a trace that passes. -/
def checkTrace (τ : Trace) : List String :=
  checkReferences τ ++ staticMap τ ++ devices τ ++ representation τ ++ geometry τ
    ++ τ.flatMap occupancy ++ pathLength τ ++ yaw τ

/-- Every defect of the witness instant: `at` is a scene's timestamp, and every grounded track and
    every entity of the case, with its declared kind, is present in that scene. -/
def checkWitness (τ : Trace) (grounding : List (String × TrackId)) (entities : List (String × Val)) (at_ms : Timestamp) : List String :=
  match τ.find? (·.t == at_ms) with
  | none => [s!"at {at_ms} is not the timestamp of any scene"]
  | some s =>
    (grounding.filterMap fun (b, t) =>
      if s.tracks.contains t then none else some s!"scene t={at_ms}: binder {b} is grounded to track {t}, which is not in this scene")
    ++ entities.filterMap fun (n, v) =>
      if present s v.kind (match v with | .track t => t | .region r => r | .device d => d) then none
      else some s!"scene t={at_ms}: entity {n} is {kindName v.kind} {match v with | .track t => t | .region r => r | .device d => d}, which is not in this scene"

end TraceLint
end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TRAINING SPLIT variant, generated by harness/tools/split.py from the full file: the lines that read the
3	  atoms the split omits are removed. Do not edit; regenerate.
4	-/
5	/-
6	  TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Primitives
7	  What the formula language cannot express, each a geometric computation with no legal word in it:
8	  a heading change integrated over a window, the closest approach of two bodies under constant
9	  velocities, the structured matching of a sign's legend. One definition per `prim.*` id of the
10	  ontology, named `prim_name`, computed over the whole trace from atoms only, parameters as
11	  arguments with no default.
12	
13	  A concept (a pipeline node) is written over atoms and primitives in the formula language and
14	  expanded before evaluation; nothing else computes a manoeuvre here. `Ctx` is the trace indexed
15	  for evaluation, shared with Semantics.lean.
16	-/
17	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Atoms
18	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.RegionTable
19	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Params
20	import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Temporal
21	import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Accumulate
22	
23	namespace TrafficSpec
24	namespace Primitives
25	open Temporal
26	
27	/-- Whether two boundaries are the same list of vertices, each coordinate compared by its
28	    numerator and denominator. -/
29	def sameBoundary : List Vec → List Vec → Bool
30	  | [], [] => true
31	  | a :: as, b :: bs =>
32	    a.1.num == b.1.num && a.1.den == b.1.den && a.2.num == b.2.num && a.2.den == b.2.den && sameBoundary as bs
33	  | _, _ => false
34	
35	theorem sameBoundary_eq : ∀ {a b : List Vec}, sameBoundary a b = true → a = b
36	  | [], [], _ => rfl
37	  | a :: as, b :: bs, h => by
38	    simp only [sameBoundary, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h
39	    obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, h3⟩, h4⟩, h5⟩ := h
40	    rcases a with ⟨⟨an1, ad1, _⟩, ⟨an2, ad2, _⟩⟩
41	    rcases b with ⟨⟨bn1, bd1, _⟩, ⟨bn2, bd2, _⟩⟩
42	    simp only at h1 h2 h3 h4
43	    subst h1 h2 h3 h4
44	    rw [sameBoundary_eq h5]
45	  | [], _ :: _, h => by simp [sameBoundary] at h
46	  | _ :: _, [], h => by simp [sameBoundary] at h
47	
48	/-- A region's boundary with its simple-polygon flag, computed the first time it is read; the flag
49	    is the direct check of that boundary by construction. -/
50	structure SimpleEntry where
51	  id : RegionId

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Primitives
  What the formula language cannot express, each a geometric computation with no legal word in it:
  a heading change integrated over a window, the closest approach of two bodies under constant
  velocities, the structured matching of a sign's legend. One definition per `prim.*` id of the
  ontology, named `prim_name`, computed over the whole trace from atoms only, parameters as
  arguments with no default.

  A concept (a pipeline node) is written over atoms and primitives in the formula language and
  expanded before evaluation; nothing else computes a manoeuvre here. `Ctx` is the trace indexed
  for evaluation, shared with Semantics.lean.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Atoms
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.RegionTable
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Params
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Temporal
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Accumulate

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Primitives
open Temporal

/-- Whether two boundaries are the same list of vertices, each coordinate compared by its
    numerator and denominator. -/
def sameBoundary : List Vec → List Vec → Bool
  | [], [] => true
  | a :: as, b :: bs =>
    a.1.num == b.1.num && a.1.den == b.1.den && a.2.num == b.2.num && a.2.den == b.2.den && sameBoundary as bs
  | _, _ => false

theorem sameBoundary_eq : ∀ {a b : List Vec}, sameBoundary a b = true → a = b
  | [], [], _ => rfl
  | a :: as, b :: bs, h => by
    simp only [sameBoundary, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at h
    obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, h3⟩, h4⟩, h5⟩ := h
    rcases a with ⟨⟨an1, ad1, _⟩, ⟨an2, ad2, _⟩⟩
    rcases b with ⟨⟨bn1, bd1, _⟩, ⟨bn2, bd2, _⟩⟩
    simp only at h1 h2 h3 h4
    subst h1 h2 h3 h4
    rw [sameBoundary_eq h5]
  | [], _ :: _, h => by simp [sameBoundary] at h
  | _ :: _, [], h => by simp [sameBoundary] at h

/-- A region's boundary with its simple-polygon flag, computed the first time it is read; the flag
    is the direct check of that boundary by construction. -/
structure SimpleEntry where
  id : RegionId
  boundary : List Vec
  flag : Thunk Bool
  ok : flag.get = Geom.simplePolygon boundary

/-- One entry per region and distinct boundary in the trace: a map's boundaries do not change from
    scene to scene, so each is checked once however many scenes and calls read it. -/
def simpleTable (scenes : Array Scene) : List SimpleEntry :=
  scenes.foldl (fun acc s => s.structures.foldl (fun acc st =>
      match st.boundary with
      | none => acc
      | some b =>
        if acc.any (fun e => e.id == st.id && sameBoundary e.boundary b) then acc
        else ⟨st.id, b, Thunk.mk (fun _ => Geom.simplePolygon b), rfl⟩ :: acc) acc) []

/-- The trace indexed for evaluation, with the run's reading. `aggregateOverrides` fixes the
    membership of a track in an aggregate to a value, for the sensitivity of a verdict to that
    membership; it is empty in every evaluation that judges a trace. -/
structure Ctx where
  scenes : Array Scene
  times : Array Q
  ρ : Reading
  aggregateOverrides : List (TrackId × String × Bool) := []
  /-- The simple-polygon flags of the trace's boundaries (`simpleIn`). -/
  simple : List SimpleEntry := simpleTable scenes
  /-- What a region quantifier reads of these scenes, built once and shared by every evaluation of
      this context (`RegionTable`). -/
  regions : RegionTable.Tables scenes := RegionTable.Tables.build scenes

/-- Whether a region's boundary is a simple polygon, read from the trace's table when the region and
    its boundary are there, checked directly otherwise. -/
def simpleIn (c : Ctx) (r : RegionId) (poly : List Vec) : Bool :=
  match c.simple.find? (fun e => e.id == r && sameBoundary e.boundary poly) with
  | some e => e.flag.get
  | none => Geom.simplePolygon poly

/-- The table never changes the answer: a hit is the direct check of the same boundary, a miss (a
    region or boundary not in the table, a boundary changed since) is the direct check. -/
theorem simpleIn_eq (c : Ctx) (r : RegionId) (poly : List Vec) : simpleIn c r poly = Geom.simplePolygon poly := by
  unfold simpleIn
  split
  · rename_i e h
    have hp := List.find?_some h
    simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at hp
    rw [e.ok, sameBoundary_eq hp.2]
  · rfl

def Ctx.mk' (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) : Ctx :=
  { scenes := τ.toArray, times := (τ.map fun s => Time.ofTimestamp s.t).toArray, ρ := ρ }
def Ctx.n (c : Ctx) : Nat := c.scenes.size

/-- An argument as the dispatcher receives it: a resolved entity id (tracks, regions and devices
    are all `Nat`), an enumeration spelling, or a natural. -/
inductive DArg
  | v (id : Nat)
  | s (lit : String)
  | n (nat : Nat)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Lifting scene functions over the trace; positions for windows
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def each (c : Ctx) (f : Scene → R) : Array R := c.scenes.map f
def eachQ (c : Ctx) (f : Scene → QR) : Array QR := c.scenes.map f
def timePos (c : Ctx) : Array (Option Q) := c.times.map some
def pathPos (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) : Array (Option Q) := c.scenes.map (kin_path_length · x)
def positions (c : Ctx) (m : Measure) (x : TrackId) : Array (Option Q) :=
  match m with | .time => timePos c | .path => pathPos c x
def missingPos (m : Measure) : UnknownReason :=
  match m with | .time => .outOfRange | .path => .absentAtom "kin_path_length"

def bAtom (o : Option Bool) (name : String) : R := R.ofOption o (.absentAtom name)
def qAtom (o : Option Q) (name : String) : QR :=
  match o with | some q => .ok q | none => .error (.absentAtom name)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Scene-level helpers over atoms

/-- Heading change (degrees, left positive) integrated over the back window of length w:
    prefix sums of yaw rate × interval, one window query per instant. -/
def yawChange (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (w : Q) : Array (Except UnknownReason Q) :=
  let n := c.n

  let sums := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Q) i =>
    let prev := if i = 0 then Q.zero else acc[i - 1]!
    let dt := if i = 0 then Q.zero else Q.sub c.times[i]! c.times[i - 1]!
    acc.push (match kin_yaw_rate c.scenes[i]! x with
      | some ω => Q.add prev (Q.mul ω dt)
      | none => prev)) #[]
  -- lastMissing[i] = latest index ≤ i with a missing yaw rate (n when none)
  let lastMissing := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
    acc.push (if (kin_yaw_rate c.scenes[i]! x).isNone then i else (if i = 0 then n else acc[i - 1]!))) #[]
  let wins := Time.backWindows (timePos c) w
  (Array.range n).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => .error .outOfRange
    | some win =>
      if !win.covered then .error (.windowTruncated "prim_heading_change")
      else if !win.adequate then .error (.samplingGap "prim_heading_change")
      else
        let lm := lastMissing[i]!

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The primitives
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- minute m of the day lies in the window [start, end), wrapping past midnight when end ≤ start. -/
def inWindow (w : TimeWindow) (m : Nat) : Bool :=
  if w.startMinute < w.endMinute then w.startMinute ≤ m && m < w.endMinute
  else m ≥ w.startMinute || m < w.endMinute

private def hasClassOpt (s : Scene) (x : TrackId) (k : RoadUserClass) : Option Bool :=
  (s.user x).bind fun u => if u.unobservedClasses.contains k then none else u.classes.map (·.contains k)

private def vecAtom (o : Option Vec) (name : String) : Except UnknownReason Vec :=
  match o with | some v => .ok v | none => .error (.absentAtom name)

/-- Under constant velocities, the time of closest approach of the two centres and the centre
    distance then; `none` when the paths do not approach within `[0, horizon]`. -/
private def closestApproach (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Except UnknownReason (Option (Q × Q)) := do
  let pa ← vecAtom (kin_position s a) "kin_position"
  let pb ← vecAtom (kin_position s b) "kin_position"
  let va ← vecAtom (kin_velocity s a) "kin_velocity"
  let vb ← vecAtom (kin_velocity s b) "kin_velocity"
  let r := Geom.vsub pb pa
  let v := Geom.vsub vb va
  let vv := Geom.dot v v
  if Q.isZero vv then pure none
  else
    let tstar := Q.neg (Q.div (Geom.dot r v) vv)
    if Q.lt tstar Q.zero || Q.gt tstar horizon then pure none
    else pure (some (tstar, Geom.norm (Geom.vadd r (Q.mul tstar v.1, Q.mul tstar v.2))))

/-- Signed heading change (degrees, left positive) over the back window w, integrated from the yaw
    rate; unknown where the window is truncated, sparsely sampled or a yaw rate is missing. -/
def prim_heading_change (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (w : Q) : Array QR :=
  (yawChange c x w).map fun e => match e with
    | .error r => .error (match r with
        | .windowTruncated _ => .windowTruncated "prim_heading_change"
        | .samplingGap _ => .samplingGap "prim_heading_change"
        | other => other)
    | .ok Δ => .ok Δ

/-- The centres approach each other within the horizon. -/
def prim_closest_approach_within (c : Ctx) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Array R :=
  each c fun s => match closestApproach s a b horizon with
    | .error w => R.u w
    | .ok o => R.ofBool o.isSome

/-- The time of closest approach; undefined when the centres do not approach within the horizon. -/
def prim_closest_approach_time (c : Ctx) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Array QR :=
  eachQ c fun s => do
    match ← closestApproach s a b horizon with
    | some (t, _) => pure t
    | none => throw (.undefined "prim_closest_approach_time")

/-- The centre distance at closest approach; undefined when the centres do not approach within the horizon. -/
def prim_closest_approach_distance (c : Ctx) (a b : TrackId) (horizon : Q) : Array QR :=
  eachQ c fun s => do
    match ← closestApproach s a b horizon with
    | some (_, dist) => pure dist
    | none => throw (.undefined "prim_closest_approach_distance")

/-- The legend conditions of device d hold now for road user x: a time window on a listed day (or a
    calendar class the scene declares), any occupancy or class condition, children present. -/
def prim_conditions_hold (c : Ctx) (d : DeviceId) (x : TrackId) : Array R :=
  each c fun s =>
    let conds := match dev_zone_sign_conditions s d with
      | some cd => some cd
      | none => dev_regulatory_sign_conditions s d
    R.bindOpt conds (.absentAtom "dev_zone_sign_conditions") fun cd =>
      let timeOk : R :=
        if cd.windows.isEmpty then R.t
        else R.bindOpt (env_civil_time s) (.absentAtom "env_civil_time") fun ct =>
          R.any (cd.windows.map fun w =>
            let dayOk : R := match w.calendarClass with
              | some cls => R.ofOption (s.assumption cls) (.assumptionMissing cls)
              | none => R.ofBool (w.weekdays.isEmpty || w.weekdays.contains ct.weekday)
            R.and dayOk (R.ofBool (inWindow w ct.minuteOfDay)))
      let occOk : R := match cd.minOccupancy with
        | none => R.t
        | some n => bAtom ((ru_occupant_count s x).map (· ≥ n)) "ru_occupant_count"
      let clsOk : R := match cd.vehicleClass with
        | none => R.t
        | some k => bAtom (hasClassOpt s x k) "ru_class"
      let childOk : R :=
        if cd.whenChildrenPresent then R.any (s.tracks.map fun y => bAtom (ru_child s y) "ru_child") else R.t
      R.and (R.and timeOk occOk) (R.and clsOk childOk)

/-- The signed lateral offset of region r from road user x (m, left positive): the component,
    perpendicular to x's heading, of the vector from x's reference point to the nearest point of
    r's boundary; zero where the reference point lies inside r. Where several boundary points are
    equally nearest, their common component; undefined where those components differ. -/
def prim_region_lateral_offset (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (r : RegionId) : Array QR :=
  eachQ c fun s => do
    let some p := kin_position s x | throw (.absentAtom "kin_position")
    let some h := kin_heading s x | throw (.absentAtom "kin_heading")
    let some poly := st_region_geometry_boundary s r | throw (.absentAtom "st_region_geometry")
    if Geom.inPolygon p poly then pure Q.zero
    else
      let lats ← (Geom.nearestPoints p poly).mapM fun q =>
        match Geom.inFrame h (Geom.vsub q p) with
        | some (_, lat) => pure lat
        | none => throw (.absentAtom "kin_heading")
      match lats with
      | [] => throw (.absentAtom "st_region_geometry")
      | l :: ls => if ls.all (Q.eq · l) then pure l else throw (.undefined "prim_region_lateral_offset")

/-- The signed distance (m) from road user x's reference point to region r, along carrier l's
    designated direction, on the line through the reference point parallel to that direction. r is
    a closed set: a vertex the line only touches and an edge it runs along are points of r it meets.
    Zero where the reference point lies in r or on its boundary; where every point of r on the line
    lies ahead, the distance to the nearest of them; where every one lies behind, minus the distance
    to the nearest. Where the line does not meet r, the value comes from r's projection on the
    direction, the interval [lo, hi] of the signed distances of r's points along it: lo where lo > 0,
    hi where hi < 0. That value is a projection gap, not a distance along the line, so the value may
    jump where the line starts or stops meeting r; its sign gives the side in both cases. Undefined
    where the line meets r both ahead and behind, where it misses r and [lo, hi] spans or touches
    zero, and where
    r's boundary is not a simple polygon (an empty list, fewer than three vertices, zero area, or a
    boundary that crosses or touches itself); unknown where the position, the direction (a zero
    vector included) or the boundary is absent. Independent of the boundary's start vertex and
    orientation. The direction is normalised as `st_lane_direction` is read (`Geom.unit`, with Core's
    micrometre-rounded square root), and the distance is counted in lengths of that normalised
    vector, which lie between 1 and 1 + 2·10⁻⁶ m. The value is geometry only: it does not establish
    that x is on l, that r marks l's entrance, that x's whole body has crossed r, or that a crossing
    happened between observations, and a distance to r is read from `st_region_geometry_distance`. -/
def prim_region_offset_along (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (r l : RegionId) : Array QR :=
  eachQ c fun s => do
    let some p := kin_position s x | throw (.absentAtom "kin_position")
    let some u := (st_lane_direction s l).bind Geom.unit | throw (.absentAtom "st_lane_direction")
    let some poly := st_region_geometry_boundary s r | throw (.absentAtom "st_region_geometry")
    if !simpleIn c r poly then throw (.undefined "prim_region_offset_along")
    let ts := Geom.lineCrossings p u poly
    if Geom.inPolygon p poly || Geom.onBoundary p poly then pure Q.zero
    else match ts with
      | [] =>
        match poly.map fun q => Q.div (Geom.dot (Geom.vsub q p) u) (Geom.dot u u) with
        | [] => throw (.undefined "prim_region_offset_along")
        | t :: rest =>
          if (t :: rest).all (Q.lt Q.zero ·) then pure (rest.foldl Q.min t)
          else if (t :: rest).all (Q.lt · Q.zero) then pure (rest.foldl Q.max t)
          else throw (.undefined "prim_region_offset_along")
      | t :: rest =>
        if ts.all (Q.lt Q.zero ·) then pure (rest.foldl Q.min t)
        else if ts.all (Q.lt · Q.zero) then pure (rest.foldl Q.max t)
        else throw (.undefined "prim_region_offset_along")

/-- Path length over which `holds` has held continuously up to each instant (`Term.distanceWhile`). -/
def distanceWhile (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (holds : Array R) : Array QR :=
  Temporal.distanceWhileAll (pathPos c x) holds

/-- Signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of road user x since ψ last became true
    (`Term.headingSince`), integrated from the yaw rate as `prim_heading_change` integrates it, with
    `maxStep` bounding every interval from the one ending at the start. -/
def headingSince (c : Ctx) (x : TrackId) (maxStep : Q) (ψ : Array R) : Array QR :=
  Accumulate.sinceRiseIntegralAll c.times (c.scenes.map (kin_yaw_rate · x)) maxStep "heading_since"
    (.absentAtom "kin_yaw_rate") ψ

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Tables and dispatch by name
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Every `prim_*` definition of this file. The doctor holds this against `primitiveIds`. -/
def primitiveNames : List String :=
  ["prim_heading_change", "prim_closest_approach_within", "prim_closest_approach_time",
   "prim_closest_approach_distance", "prim_conditions_hold", "prim_region_lateral_offset",
   "prim_region_offset_along"]

/-- The atoms each primitive reads (Lean names of Atoms.lean); Manifest.lean turns a primitive
    into the atoms a source must observe. -/
def reads (n : String) : List String :=

  | "prim_closest_approach_within" | "prim_closest_approach_time" | "prim_closest_approach_distance" => ["kin_position", "kin_velocity"]

  | "prim_region_lateral_offset" => ["kin_position", "kin_heading", "st_region_geometry"]
  | "prim_region_offset_along" => ["kin_position", "st_lane_direction", "st_region_geometry"]
  | _ => []

/-- The sort each entity argument of a primitive must have (`none` marks a literal or natural
    position). The static check holds variables to these. -/

  | "prim_conditions_hold" => some [some EntityKind.device, t]
  | "prim_region_lateral_offset" => some [t, some EntityKind.region]
  | "prim_region_offset_along" => some [t, some EntityKind.region, some EntityKind.region]
  | _ => none

private def tid (a : DArg) : Except UnknownReason TrackId :=
  match a with | .v t => .ok t | .n n => .ok n | _ => .error (.malformed "entity")

/-- A name no primitive carries: a concept call that no expansion replaced, or a misspelling. -/

2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Adequacy
3	  Mutation adequacy of a rule's witnesses: every leaf of the applicability and the obligation
4	  must do some work in some witness. A leaf is replaced by `tt` and by `ff` in turn; if neither
5	  replacement changes any scenario's episode verdict, the leaf is unexercised — the witnesses do
6	  not show that it matters, and a rule could carry an irrelevant atom without anyone noticing.
7	  Only the witnesses that expect a decided verdict count: a witness that expects unknown under a
8	  mask is decided by blanking any leaf that reads the masked atom, so it exercises nothing.

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Adequacy
  Mutation adequacy of a rule's witnesses: every leaf of the applicability and the obligation
  must do some work in some witness. A leaf is replaced by `tt` and by `ff` in turn; if neither
  replacement changes any scenario's episode verdict, the leaf is unexercised — the witnesses do
  not show that it matters, and a rule could carry an irrelevant atom without anyone noticing.
  Only the witnesses that expect a decided verdict count: a witness that expects unknown under a
  mask is decided by blanking any leaf that reads the masked atom, so it exercises nothing.

  A concept call is one leaf: the rule's witnesses must show the concept matters, and the
  concept's own witnesses exercise its body.

  Leaves of one atom that differ only in a literal argument (the values of one enumeration, each
  tested in its own disjunct) are one leaf in meaning: the family is unexercised only when none of
  its members moves a witness, and it is reported once.

  Only the gate reads this file; rules never import it.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Adequacy

/-- The verdict tag one scenario produces for a rule: the episode verdict's tag, or the whole error. -/
def tagOf (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (cs : List Concept) (sc : Scenario) : String :=
  match sc.run ((rules.filter (·.id != r.id)) ++ [r]) cs with
  | .ok v => v.tag
  | .error e => s!"error:{e}"

/-- The verdict tags a scenario list produces for a rule. -/
def profile (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (scs : List Scenario) (cs : List Concept := []) : List String :=
  scs.map (tagOf rules r cs)

/-- Whether the scenarios' tags for `r` differ from `base`, their tags for the unchanged rule
    (`profile rules r scs cs != base`), decided at the first scenario whose tag differs. -/
def moves (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (cs : List Concept) : List Scenario → List String → Bool
  | sc :: scs, b :: bs => if tagOf rules r cs sc != b then true else moves rules r cs scs bs
  | [], [] => false
  | _, _ => true

/-- A leaf's family: its description with every literal argument blanked, so the leaves that
    test the values of one enumeration on the same atom and variables share a family. -/
def family (leaf : String) : String :=
  let marker := "Arg.lit \""
  match leaf.splitOn marker with
  | [] => leaf
  | first :: rest =>
    rest.foldl (fun acc piece =>
      let after := (piece.splitOn "\"").drop 1      -- drop the literal's text, keep what follows its closing quote
      acc ++ marker ++ "_\"" ++ "\"".intercalate after) first

/-- One part's report, given its leaves (`names`, in order) and which of them move a witness: a
    family of literal variants counts once and only when no member moves, reported at its first
    leaf with the count of its members. A family's members are asked in order, and the first that
    moves settles it. -/
def report (label : String) (names : List String) (moved : Nat → Bool) : List String :=
  let fams := names.map family
  let firsts := (List.range names.length).filter fun k => !((fams.take k).contains (fams[k]?.getD ""))
  firsts.filterMap fun k =>
    let fam := fams[k]?.getD ""
    let members := (List.range names.length).filter fun j => fams[j]?.getD "" == fam
    if members.any moved then none
    else
      let note := if members.length > 1 then s!" (one of {members.length} literal variants of this atom; none exercised)" else ""
      some s!"{label} leaf {k}: {names[k]?.getD ""}{note}"

/-- Leaves of the applicability and the obligation (binder classes are exercised by the
    grounding itself) that neither `tt` nor `ff` replacement moves any witness on, reported by
    `report`. -/
def unexercised (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (scs : List Scenario) (cs : List Concept := []) : List String :=
  let decided := scs.filter fun sc => sc.expected.tag != "unknown"
  let base := profile rules r decided cs
  let check (label : String) (get : Rule → Formula) (put : Rule → Formula → Rule) : List String :=
    let φ := get r
    report label (Formula.leaves φ) fun k => [Formula.tt, Formula.ff].any fun rep =>
      moves rules (put r (Formula.replaceLeaf k rep φ)) cs decided base
  check "applicability" (·.applicability) (fun r φ => { r with applicability := φ }) ++
  check "obligation" (·.obligation) (fun r φ => { r with obligation := φ })

end Adequacy
end TrafficSpec

5	/-
6	  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Manifest
7	  What a source can observe: a capability per atom id, complete over ATOMS.md (`subject` is an atom
8	  observed for the subject track alone, as an instrumented vehicle reports its own controls); a mask
9	  that blanks every field of an absent atom, and of a subject-only atom on every other road user,
10	  before evaluation; and `support`, the first and most honest number
11	  a source gets — which rules it can be judged against at all, computed from the rules' syntax
12	  before any frame is read.
13	
14	  The same rules run on a simulator, on an annotated dataset and on perception over video; the
15	  only thing that differs is what each can see, and that difference is a declared input here.
16	  For the perception stage the manifest is the interface the other way round: the list of atoms
17	  its programs must deliver, with the error class each is allowed.
18	-/
19	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
20	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Semantics
21	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Ontology.Ids
22	
23	namespace TrafficSpec
24	
25	inductive Capability
26	  | exact
27	  | estimate (errorClass : String)
28	  | absent
29	  | subject
30	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
31	
32	structure Manifest where
33	  source : String
34	  entries : List (String × Capability)     -- atom id in ATOMS.md form ↦ capability
35	  /-- The longest tracker break the source's re-identification links may bridge (seconds). -/
36	  reidGap : Q := Q.zero
37	  deriving Repr, Inhabited
38	
39	namespace Manifest
40	/-- An atom the manifest does not list is absent: silence is not a capability. -/
41	def capability (m : Manifest) (id : String) : Capability :=
42	  ((m.entries.find? (·.1 == id)).map (·.2)).getD .absent
43	def observes (m : Manifest) (id : String) : Bool := m.capability id != .absent
44	/-- Complete: every atom id of ATOMS.md has an entry, and no entry names anything else. -/
45	def complete (m : Manifest) : Bool :=
46	  atomIds.all (fun id => (m.entries.find? (·.1 == id)).isSome) &&
47	  m.entries.all (fun e => atomIds.contains e.1)
48	def absentIds (m : Manifest) : List String := atomIds.filter fun id => !m.observes id
49	/-- The atoms observed for the subject track only. -/
50	def subjectIds (m : Manifest) : List String := atomIds.filter fun id => m.capability id == .subject
51	/-- A manifest that observes everything exactly (the simulator's, and the tests'). -/
52	def full (source : String) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
53	  { source := source, entries := atomIds.map fun id => (id, .exact), reidGap := gap }
54	end Manifest
55	
56	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	-- From Lean names back to atom ids
58	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	/-- The atom id a Lean name reads: the longest id whose `defName` is a prefix of the name
60	    (`dev_traffic_signal_shows` ↦ `dev.traffic_signal`), with the relation aliases spelled out. -/
61	def atomIdOf (name : String) : Option String :=
62	  let n := match name with
63	    | "rel_ahead_in_lane" | "rel_behind_in_lane" => "rel_ahead_behind_in_lane"
64	    | other => other
65	  let cands := atomIds.filter fun id =>
66	    let d := Semantics.defName id
67	    n == d || n.startsWith (d ++ "_")
68	  cands.foldl (fun acc id => match acc with
69	    | none => some id
70	    | some a => if id.length > a.length then some id else some a) none
71	
72	/-- The atom ids a read of `id` depends on: itself, and for a read of a region kind or of a relation
73	    that reads kind membership, the kinds whose masks its verdict follows (a kind's ancestors; a
74	    lane relation's lane kind; an entrance's line kinds, stop line and crosswalk). No source
75	    declares an abstract kind: a read of one depends on the kinds refining it directly, and no read
76	    depends on an abstract ancestor. -/
77	def kindDependencies (id : String) : List String :=
78	  let kinds (ks : List StructureKind) := (ks.filter (!·.isAbstract)).map fun k => s!"st.{k}"
79	  let ofKind (k : StructureKind) :=
80	    if k.isAbstract then kinds (StructureKind.all.filter (·.parent? == some k))
81	    else kinds (k :: k.ancestors)
82	  match id with
83	  | "rel.ahead_behind_in_lane" => id :: ofKind .lane
84	  | "st.entrance_of" => id :: ofKind .stopLine ++ ofKind .crosswalk
85	  | _ =>
86	    if id.startsWith "st." then
87	      match StructureKind.ofString ((id.drop 3).toString) with
88	      | some k => ofKind k
89	      | none => [id]
90	    else [id]
91	
92	/-- The atom ids a formula list reads, through atoms and primitives (a concept call is expanded first). -/
93	def formulaAtomIds (fs : List Formula) : List String :=
94	  ((fs.flatMap Formula.atoms).flatMap fun n =>
95	    if n.startsWith "prim_" then (Primitives.reads n).filterMap atomIdOf
96	    else (atomIdOf n).toList).flatMap kindDependencies |>.eraseDups
97	
98	/-- The atom ids a rule reads, through its atoms, its primitives and, transitively, the
99	    rules it composes. -/
100	def Rule.atomIds (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : List String :=
101	  let rec go (fuel : Nat) (seen : List String) (r : Rule) : List String :=
102	    match fuel with
103	    | 0 => formulaAtomIds r.formulas
104	    | fuel + 1 =>
105	      formulaAtomIds r.formulas ++ (r.composes.flatMap fun id =>
106	        if seen.contains id then [] else
107	        match rules.find? (·.id == id) with
108	        | some r' => go fuel (id :: seen) r'
109	        | none => [])
110	  (go rules.length [r.id] r).eraseDups
111	
112	inductive Support
113	  | supported
114	  | partially (absent : List String)      -- some atoms unobserved: verdicts may be unknown
115	  | unsupported (absent : List String)    -- the obligation reads nothing the source observes
116	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
117	
118	def Support.tag : Support → String
119	  | .supported => "supported"
120	  | .partially _ => "partial"
121	  | .unsupported _ => "unsupported"
122	def Support.absent : Support → List String
123	  | .supported => []
124	  | .partially a | .unsupported a => a
125	
126	/-- Support from syntax alone, closed over the rules a rule composes. Unsupported when every atom
127	    the obligation reads is absent (the rule could never decide), or a binder's class can never be
128	    established, or a composed rule is itself unsupported. -/
129	def support (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (m : Manifest) : Support :=
130	  -- the clock is every source's: a window over time reads it, and no manifest declares it absent
131	  let absentOf (fs : List Formula) : List String × Nat :=
132	    let ids := (formulaAtomIds fs).filter (· != "kin.time")
133	    (ids.filter fun id => !m.observes id, ids.length)
134	  let (oblAbsent, oblTotal) := absentOf [r.obligation]
135	  let clsDead := r.binders.any fun b =>
136	    let (a, n) := absentOf [b.cls]
137	    n > 0 && a.length == n
138	  let composedDead := (r.composes.filterMap fun id => rules.find? (·.id == id)).any fun r' =>
139	    let (a, n) := absentOf [r'.obligation]
140	    n > 0 && a.length == n
141	  let allAbsent := (Rule.atomIds rules r).filter fun id => !m.observes id
142	  if allAbsent.isEmpty then .supported
143	  else if clsDead || composedDead || (oblTotal > 0 && oblAbsent.length == oblTotal) then .unsupported allAbsent
144	  else .partially allAbsent
145	
146	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
147	-- Masking: a scene as the source would have produced it
148	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
149	namespace Mask
150	def user (id : String) (u : RoadUser) : RoadUser :=
151	  match id with
152	  | "ru.subject" => u
153	  | "ru.occupant_count" => { u with occupants := none }
154	  | "ru.rider_posture" => { u with posture := {} }
155	  | "kin.position" => { u with kin := { u.kin with position := none } }
156	  | "kin.heading" => { u with kin := { u.kin with heading := none } }
157	  | "kin.velocity" => { u with kin := { u.kin with velocity := none } }
158	  | "kin.speed" => { u with kin := { u.kin with speed := none } }
159	  | "kin.accel_longitudinal" => { u with kin := { u.kin with accelLongitudinal := none } }
160	  | "kin.yaw_rate" => { u with kin := { u.kin with yawRate := none } }
161	  | "kin.extent" => { u with kin := { u.kin with extent := none } }
162	  | "kin.steer_angle" => { u with kin := { u.kin with steerAngle := none } }
163	  | "kin.path_length" => { u with kin := { u.kin with pathLength := none } }
164	  | "kin.engine_running" => { u with kin := { u.kin with engineRunning := none } }
165	  | "kin.parking_brake" => { u with kin := { u.kin with parkingBrake := none } }
166	  | "kin.gear" => { u with kin := { u.kin with gear := none } }
167	  | "kin.throttle" => { u with kin := { u.kin with throttle := none } }
168	  | "kin.service_brake" => { u with kin := { u.kin with serviceBrake := none } }
169	  | "sig.turn_indicator" => { u with sig := { u.sig with turnIndicator := none } }
170	  | "sig.brake_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with brakeLamp := none } }
171	  | "sig.hazard" => { u with sig := { u.sig with hazard := none } }
172	  | "sig.headlamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with headlamp := none } }
173	  | "sig.position_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with positionLamp := none } }
174	  | "sig.warning_lamp" => { u with sig := { u.sig with warningLamps := none } }
175	  | "sig.siren" => { u with sig := { u.sig with siren := none } }
176	  | "sig.horn" => { u with sig := { u.sig with horn := none } }
177	  | "sig.hand_signal" => { u with sig := { u.sig with handSignal := none } }
178	  | "ru.aggregate" => { u with classes := none }   -- the source classifies nothing: every member unknown
179	  | "sig.door_open" => { u with sig := { u.sig with doorsOpen := none } }
180	  | "sig.compression_brake" => { u with sig := { u.sig with compressionBrake := none } }
181	  | "st.sight_along_way" => { u with sightAlongWay := none }
182	  | _ =>
183	    -- a class atom: the source cannot tell this class, so no user is known to have or lack it,
184	    -- nor the attribute the class carries

186	    | some k =>

188	      match k with

190	      | .officialVehicle => { u with officialKind := none }
191	      | .electricBicycle => { u with eBikeClass := none }
192	      | _ => u
193	    | none => u
194	
195	def structure' (id : String) (st : Structure) : Option Structure :=
196	  match id with
197	  | "st.lane_direction" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with direction := none } }
198	  | "st.lane_adjacency" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l =>
199	      { l with leftNeighbour := none, rightNeighbour := none, ordinalFromLeft := none, countInDirection := none } }
200	  | "st.lane_connectivity" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with leadsTo := none } }
201	  | "st.lane_enters" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with entersIntersection := none } }
202	  | "st.lane_marking" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with markingLeft := none, markingRight := none } }
203	  | "st.lane_width" => some { st with lane := st.lane.map fun l => { l with width := none } }
204	  | "st.curvature" => some { st with curvature := none }
205	  | "st.grade" => some { st with grade := none }
206	  | "st.sight_distance" => some { st with sightDistance := none }
207	  | "st.on_way" => some { st with ways := none }
208	  | "st.entrance_of" => some { st with entranceOf := [], entranceObserved := false }
209	  | "st.region_geometry" => some { st with position := none, boundary := none }

214	    match StructureKind.ofString ((id.drop 3).toString) with
215	    | some k => if k.isAbstract then some st else some { st with unobservedKinds := k :: st.unobservedKinds }
216	    | none => some st
217	
218	def device (id : String) (d : Device) : Option Device :=
219	  match id with
220	  | "dev.governs" => some { d with governs := [], governsObserved := false }
221	  | "dev.position" => some { d with position := none }
222	  | "dev.inoperative" => some { d with inoperative := none }
223	  | _ =>
224	    -- a kind atom: the source cannot tell this kind, so no device is known to be or not be one
225	    match DeviceKind.ofString ((id.drop 4).toString) with
226	    | some k => some { d with unobservedKinds := k :: d.unobservedKinds }
227	    | none => some d
228	
229	def env (id : String) (e : Env) : Env :=
230	  match id with
231	  | "env.darkness" => { e with darkness := none }
232	  | "env.precipitation" => { e with precipitation := none }
233	  | "env.wet_road" => { e with wetRoad := none }
234	  | "env.ice_or_snow" => { e with iceOrSnow := none }
235	  | "env.visibility" => { e with visibility := none }
236	  | "env.civil_time" => { e with civilTime := none }
237	  | _ => e
238	
239	def relation (id : String) (m : MeasuredRelation) : MeasuredRelation :=
240	  match id with
241	  | "rel.centre_distance" => { m with centreDistance := none }
242	  | "rel.surface_gap" => { m with surfaceGap := none }
243	  | "rel.ahead_behind_in_lane" => { m with aAheadOfB := none }
244	  | "rel.longitudinal_overlap" => { m with longitudinalOverlap := none }
245	  | "rel.oncoming" => { m with oncoming := none }
246	  | "rel.same_direction" => { m with sameDirection := none }
247	  | "rel.bearing" => { m with bearing := none }
248	  | "rel.contact" => { m with contact := none }
249	  | "rel.visible" => { m with visible := none }
250	  | _ => m
251	
252	/-- Blank one atom in a scene. The computed relations are blanked through the kinematics they
253	    would be computed from only when the source lacks those too; a measured value is dropped. -/
254	def scene (id : String) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
255	  match id with
256	  | "ru.subject" => { s with subject := none }
257	  | "rel.occupies" => { s with occupancyObserved := [], occupies := [] }
258	  | "kin.time" => s
259	  | _ =>
260	    { s with users := s.users.map (user id)
261	             structures := s.structures.filterMap (structure' id)
262	             devices := s.devices.filterMap (device id)
263	             env := env id s.env
264	             relations := s.relations.map (relation id) }
265	
266	/-- Blank one atom on every road user but the subject, and in every measured relation not taken
267	    from the subject: what a source that instruments the subject's vehicle alone can say. -/
268	def sceneExceptSubject (id : String) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
269	  { s with users := s.users.map fun u => if s.subject == some u.track then u else user id u
270	           relations := s.relations.map fun m => if s.subject == some m.a then m else relation id m }
271	end Mask
272	
273	/-- The scene as the source would have produced it: every absent atom blanked, every subject-only
274	    atom blanked on everyone but the subject. -/
275	def mask (m : Manifest) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
276	  let s := m.absentIds.foldl (fun acc id => Mask.scene id acc) s
277	  m.subjectIds.foldl (fun acc id => Mask.sceneExceptSubject id acc) s
278	def maskTrace (m : Manifest) (τ : Trace) : Trace := τ.map (mask m)

def sqrtMicro (q : Q) : Q :=
  if q.num ≤ 0 then Q.zero
  else
    let scaled : Int := (q.num * 1000000000000) / (q.den : Int)   -- µm²
    Units.micrometres (Int.ofNat (isqrt scaled.toNat))
def norm (a : Vec) : Q := sqrtMicro (normSq a)
/-- The unit vector along `a`; `none` for the zero vector only. `a` is first divided by its larger
    absolute component, so the vector normalised has length between 1 and √2 whatever `a`'s scale,
    and then by that length taken to micrometres (`norm`). The result is the exact unit vector times
    a factor of at least 1 and below 1 + 2·10⁻⁶, and is exact where the scaled length is a whole
    number of micrometres (every axis-aligned direction). -/
def unit (a : Vec) : Option Vec :=
  let m := Q.max (Q.abs a.1) (Q.abs a.2)
  if Q.isZero m then none
  else
    let b := (Q.div a.1 m, Q.div a.2 m)
    let n := norm b
    some (Q.div b.1 n, Q.div b.2 n)
/-- Components of `v` in the frame of heading `h` (longitudinal, lateral); lateral positive = left.
    `h` is read as a direction (`unit`), whatever its length; `v` keeps its own. -/
def inFrame (h v : Vec) : Option (Q × Q) := do
  let u ← unit h

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Relations between road users. Measured where the source supplies them, otherwise computed
-- from kinematics. `none` when a needed kinematic is missing.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def rel_centre_distance (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.centreDistance) with
  | some d => some d
  | none => do
    let pa ← kin_position s a
    let pb ← kin_position s b
    pure (Geom.norm (Geom.vsub pb pa))

/-- Components of `b`'s position relative to `a` in `a`'s heading frame (longitudinal, lateral). -/
private def relFrame (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option (Q × Q) := do
  let pa ← kin_position s a
  let pb ← kin_position s b
  let ha ← kin_heading s a
  Geom.inFrame ha (Geom.vsub pb pa)

/-- The gap between the two bodies: the vector from the nearest point of `a`'s footprint to the
    nearest point of `b`'s, each footprint read with its own heading and extent, given as its
    lengths along and across `a`'s heading (longitudinal, lateral). Neither is ever negative; both
    are zero exactly when the footprints touch or overlap. `none` when either footprint is not
    observed, and when a supplied gap has a negative component. -/
def rel_surface_gap (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option (Q × Q) :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.surfaceGap) with
  | some g => if Q.isNonneg g.1 && Q.isNonneg g.2 then some g else none
  | none => do
    let fa ← footprint s a
    let fb ← footprint s b
    let d ← Geom.nearestOffset fa fb
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let (lon, lat) ← Geom.inFrame ha d
    pure (Q.abs lon, Q.abs lat)
def rel_surface_gap_longitudinal (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q := (rel_surface_gap s a b).map (·.1)
def rel_surface_gap_lateral (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q := (rel_surface_gap s a b).map (·.2)
/-- The distance between the nearest points of the two bodies, the gap's length: zero on contact
    or overlap, never negative. -/
def rel_surface_gap_distance (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q := (rel_surface_gap s a b).map Geom.norm

/-- `a` and `b` share a lane and `a` is ahead of `b` along `a`'s heading. The lane is any region both
    occupy that is of kind lane (`Structure.isOfKind`): unknown when `a` is ahead and no shared region
    is known to be a lane but one may be. -/
def rel_ahead_behind_in_lane (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.aAheadOfB) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let ra ← rel_occupies_regions s a
    let rb ← rel_occupies_regions s b
    let (lon, _) ← relFrame s a b
    if !Q.lt lon Q.zero then some false
    else
      let shared := (s.structures.filter fun st => ra.contains st.id && rb.contains st.id).map (·.isOfKind .lane)
      if shared.contains (some true) then some true
      else if shared.contains none then none
      else some false
def rel_ahead_in_lane (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := rel_ahead_behind_in_lane s a b
def rel_behind_in_lane (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := rel_ahead_behind_in_lane s b a

/-- Signed overlap of the two footprints along `a`'s heading, each read with its own heading and
    extent: the length their projections on that axis share, positive when the bodies are side by
    side, otherwise the gap between the projections negated. A projection: it reads nothing across
    the axis, so a positive value is no contact and a negative one no distance between the bodies. -/
def rel_longitudinal_overlap (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Q :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.longitudinalOverlap) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let pa ← kin_position s a
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let u ← Geom.unit ha
    let fa ← footprint s a
    let fb ← footprint s b
    let (loA, hiA) ← Geom.span u pa fa
    let (loB, hiB) ← Geom.span u pa fb
    pure (Q.sub (Q.min hiA hiB) (Q.max loA loB))

/-- Headings opposed (cosine below `-cosTol`) and the distance decreasing. -/
def rel_oncoming (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (cosTol : Q) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.oncoming) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let hb ← kin_heading s b
    let pa ← kin_position s a
    let pb ← kin_position s b
    let va ← kin_velocity s a
    let vb ← kin_velocity s b
    let ua ← Geom.unit ha
    let ub ← Geom.unit hb
    let closing := Q.lt (Geom.dot (Geom.vsub pb pa) (Geom.vsub vb va)) Q.zero
    pure (Q.lt (Geom.dot ua ub) (Q.neg cosTol) && closing)

/-- Headings aligned (cosine above `cosTol`). -/
def rel_same_direction (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) (cosTol : Q) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.sameDirection) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => do
    let ha ← kin_heading s a
    let hb ← kin_heading s b
    let ua ← Geom.unit ha
    let ub ← Geom.unit hb
    pure (Q.gt (Geom.dot ua ub) cosTol)

/-- `b` relative to `a` in `a`'s frame: (longitudinal, lateral), lateral positive to the left. -/
def rel_bearing (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Vec :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.bearing) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => relFrame s a b
def rel_bearing_right (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.lt v.2 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_left (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.gt v.2 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_ahead (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.gt v.1 Q.zero
def rel_bearing_behind (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool := (rel_bearing s a b).map fun v => Q.lt v.1 Q.zero

/-- The bodies touch or overlap. -/
def rel_contact (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option Bool :=
  match (s.relation a b).bind (·.contact) with
  | some v => some v
  | none => (rel_surface_gap s a b).map fun g => Q.le g.1 Q.zero && Q.le g.2 Q.zero

# NRS_484B_363_4 — task result

## Final verdict

**WITNESS_FAIL** on the files as left: `blind: expected unknown, got violated; the manifest masks rel.bearing`.
Every other check passes. A diagnostic run with a substitute `blind` witness returned `OK` (18 witnesses).
That substitute was not left in the files (see below). **The node is wrong in its `blind` scenario.**

## Gate runs

1. (Accidental) The gate command ran with its output discarded while I was reading Core, on the
   harness skeleton. I did not see its verdict. It may have used one run of the budget.
2. **WITNESS_FAIL**: `blind` expected unknown, got violated. All other witnesses matched. I read
   `Core/Vocab/Atoms.lean` and `Core/Runtime/Manifest.lean` to find the cause (below).
3. **OK**, a diagnostic run. I replaced `blind` with a trace in which b's `kin.position` is unobserved
   and the bearing and longitudinal overlap are supplied as measured. This shows that the rule,
   the 17 other witnesses, the static checks, anchoring and mutation adequacy all pass. That
   `blind` is unknown because b's position is missing, not because of the mask: the pass concept
   reads `kin.position` and is unknown with or without the mask. That breaks "blind needs the
   masked atom to be the one that decides", so I reverted to the planned `blind` (forbid's trace
   with `rel.bearing` masked). The harness re-run will therefore report WITNESS_FAIL on `blind`.

## Why the node is wrong (scenario `blind`, masked `["rel.bearing"]`)

- `rel_bearing` (`Core/Vocab/Atoms.lean:635`) uses a measured bearing if the source supplies one.
  Otherwise it computes the bearing from `kin.position` of both road users and `kin.heading` of the
  subject (`relFrame`).
- Masking `rel.bearing` (`Manifest.lean`, `Mask.relation`) drops only the measured value. Computed
  relations are blanked "only when the source lacks those [kinematics] too".
- A witness may not supply a relation Core can compute. So on any witness whose kinematics are
  observed, the bearing is still computed, the mask changes nothing, and `blind` gets forbid's
  verdict (violated).
- `drv.interaction.overtake_pass` reads `kin.position` and `kin.heading` itself. Any trace that
  removes what `rel_bearing` is computed from also leaves the pass undecided. So no witness can
  make the `rel.bearing` mask the deciding unknown.

**What the plan agent must change:** mask an atom whose absence actually blanks the pass and its
occasion. For example `kin.position`: it blanks the concept, the computed `rel.bearing` and
`rel.longitudinal_overlap`, and the occupancy footprint. Or `kin.heading`. Alternatively, drop
`rel.bearing` as the blind atom: on this Core it is unobservable only where the pass concept is too.
Nothing else in the node needs to change: with a feasible blind scenario the rule and the other
witnesses already pass (run 3).

## How the rule is written (choices the node left open)

- **Under way (U).** U is `since (moving ∧ (¬behind ∨ rises behind)) (ahead ∧ aligned ∧ moving)`,
  built from the under_way element's atoms: `kin.speed` against `p.halt_speed_tolerance`;
  `rel.bearing` ahead/behind; `rel.longitudinal_overlap` < 0; `rel.same_direction` with
  `p.overtake_same_direction_cos`. `someMoment` and `throughout` are exactly the 6b forms with
  W = `p.overtake_window`.
  - U is read at each observation of the window and cannot see the judged observation. So it marks
    every observation from one where b was ahead and aligned with the moving subject, up to and
    including the first observation with b behind.
  - At a recognition, the last such stretch begins at the record's "last observation at which b was
    ahead". Earlier ahead-and-aligned observations of the moving subject (its approach) also count
    as under way.
  - The language has no operator for the stretch "from the last ψ in the window to the judged
    observation" at each of its observations, so this is the closest pointwise form. The repair
    session should know that it slightly widens the occasion.
- **"With no other vehicle in the scene the duty is met."** Written as a disjunct of the
  applicability, `¬∃b (vehicle b ∧ ¬same b subject)`, so `permit` is compliant.
- **Applicability and obligation.** The applicability is `noOther ∨ ∃b occasion(b)`. The obligation
  is `∀b (occasion(b) → ¬overtake_pass(subject, b))`, which repeats the whole selection of b, z and
  r. occasion(b) is:
  - b is another vehicle;
  - b is travelling at some moment under way;
  - a school or school_crossing zone sign z, not an end sign, governs a travel region r that the
    subject occupies at some moment under way;
  - none of exceptions (a)–(d) holds throughout.
- **Exceptions (c) and (d).** Both read "operational beacon governing r" as
  `dev_governs(bc, r) ∧ ¬dev_inoperative(bc)`, quantified over `speed_limit_beacon` devices.
- No narrowings were declared. The record's own observable readings are not restated.
- **Witnesses.**
  - `branch_4` was added (violated): an operational beacon that is not flashing, but the pupils
    are not in class. It exercises the obligation's `asm.pupils_in_class` leaf.
  - Every witness judges t = 12–19 s, so the 10 s windows are covered. Before that both vehicles
    are at rest, so no pass is under way: those observations stand for "before the pass begins" in
    the `occasion_*_outside` witnesses.

## Why I finished

The only remaining failure is the `blind` scenario, which no honest witness can satisfy on this
Core (explained above). That is a defect of the node's plan, not of the rule. I left the honest
planned `blind` witness in place, not a substitute that passes for the wrong reason.

- The pass concept `drv.interaction.overtake_pass` reads the same position and heading. Any trace that removes them leaves the pass undecided whether or not `rel.bearing` is masked, so the masked atom can never be what decides the verdict.

I stopped with the node failing the gate: the files as left return **WITNESS_FAIL** on the `blind` witness. That witness can't pass honestly, because the node planned it wrong. Everything else passes. A diagnostic run with a substitute `blind` witness returned `OK` across 18 witnesses. That substitute only passed for the wrong reason, so I put the planned `blind` back.

**Why the node is wrong:**
- `blind` masks `rel.bearing` and expects unknown.
- Core computes `rel_bearing` from `kin.position` and `kin.heading` (`Core/Vocab/Atoms.lean:635`). The mask only removes a bearing the source measured, and a witness may not supply one Core can compute. On any trace with observed movement data, the mask therefore changes nothing, and `blind` comes out violated like `forbid`.
- The pass concept `drv.interaction.overtake_pass` reads the same position and heading. Any trace that removes them leaves the pass undecided whether or not `rel.bearing` is masked, so the masked atom can never be what decides the verdict.
- **What the plan should change:** mask `kin.position` (or `kin.heading`) in `blind`, since that removes the pass and the bearing together. Nothing else in the node needs to change.

**Gate runs:**
- I accidentally ran the gate once early, on the harness-written files, with its output thrown away; it may have used one run of the budget.
- Run 2 gave WITNESS_FAIL, on `blind` only.
- Run 3 was the diagnostic `OK`. Its `blind` was undecided only because b's position was missing, which breaks the rule that the masked atom must decide.

The closest form also counts earlier observations where b was ahead with headings aligned while the subject moved (the approach). This makes the duty apply slightly more widely than the record states.
- **No other vehicle:** "With no other vehicle in the scene the duty is met" is a separate branch of the applicability, so `permit` is compliant.
